about: Contract C0 section 5. Every reader runs every case: Monet readLoraRunRef(ref, key, nowUnix), Deploy verify_lora_ref(ref, secret=key, deployment_id=, now=), the node parse_lora_ref(ref). expect is ok or the reason code. Where expect is ok and claims is present, the reader returns exactly those claims. The keys here are published fixture values.

mint.about: Monet mintLoraRunRef(claims, key) must return exactly ref, byte for byte.

cases.name: valid
cases.note: A fresh reference minted 2 hours before expiry. Every reader accepts it and returns these claims.

cases.name: valid_last_second
cases.note: nowUnix is e minus 1: still valid.

cases.name: expired_at_e
cases.note: nowUnix equals e: expired. Valid means nowUnix < e. The node never checks expiry.

cases.name: expired_later
cases.note: An hour past expiry.

cases.name: wrong_key
cases.note: Verified with a different key. The node holds no key, so it only checks shape.

cases.name: tampered_payload
cases.note: The payload was re encoded with a different size and the old signature kept.

cases.name: tampered_signature
cases.note: One signature character changed. Still canonical base64url, so the failure is the MAC, not the shape.

cases.name: wrong_deployment
cases.note: A valid reference queued on another deployment. Only Deploy knows the run's deployment; Monet's reader returns the claims.

cases.name: lifetime_at_limit
cases.note: e minus nowUnix is 7500, the most a reader accepts (7200 plus 300 seconds of clock skew).

cases.name: lifetime_too_long
cases.note: e minus nowUnix is 7501: refused even though the signature is good.

cases.name: foreign_root_signed
cases.note: Signed, but p is outside the monet/ grammar.

cases.name: traversal_signed
cases.note: Signed, but p carries a parent segment.

cases.name: sha12_mismatch_signed
cases.note: Signed, but the 12 hex in p are not the first 12 of h.

cases.name: extra_key_signed
cases.note: Signed payload with a seventh key.

cases.name: whitespace_signed
cases.note: Signed payload with a space: not the canonical serialization.

cases.name: key_order_signed
cases.note: Signed payload with keys out of the order p, h, n, d, e, u.

cases.name: uppercase_hash_signed
cases.note: h must be 64 lowercase hex.

cases.name: size_below_min_signed
cases.note: n below 16384.

cases.name: size_above_max_signed
cases.note: n above 629145600 (600 MiB, LORA_MAX_BYTES).

cases.name: deployment_uppercase_signed
cases.note: d must be a lowercase canonical uuid.

cases.name: http_source_signed
cases.note: u must be https.

cases.name: float_expiry_signed
cases.note: e must be an integer.

cases.name: non_ascii_signed
cases.note: The payload must be ASCII.

cases.name: unicode_escape_signed
cases.note: Signed, and p carries a \u escape of a non ASCII character (e acute). All three readers refuse, with different codes: JavaScript's JSON.stringify writes the character raw, so Monet's step 4 re-serialisation fails first (shape); Python's ensure_ascii writes the escape back, so Deploy and the node reach step 5 (path).

cases.name: noncanonical_bad_path_signed
cases.note: Signed, with a space in the payload AND p outside the monet/ grammar. Step 4 (canonical bytes) runs before step 5 (path) in every reader, so all three answer shape, never path.

cases.name: bad_prefix
cases.note: Wrong version prefix.

cases.name: two_segments
cases.note: No signature segment.

cases.name: padded_payload
cases.note: Base64url padding is not allowed.

cases.name: empty
cases.note: Empty string.

cases.name: plain_url
cases.note: A URL is not a reference; the run gate decides URLs separately.

cases.name: too_long
cases.note: Longer than 4096 characters.
